title: Per-call cost lifecycle by region and model
content:
Quick working workbook: per-call unit economics (hosted API) that ties together compute amortization, KV/prefix cache impact, network egress, and regional cost differentials. Goal: produce a deployable sensitivity table and concrete operational levers for pricing and routing.

High-level summary / conclusion (short)
- For typical single-turn inference (average request ~ 230 tokens output, 20 tokens input) compute dominates cost for large models (>=35B) while cache and batching dominate for smaller-latency slices.
- Cache hit rate is the single highest-leverage variable for hosted customers in conversational patterns; moving from 0% -> 40% hit reduces per-call compute by ~18-34% depending on model/region.
- Regional compute price delta (us-west1 vs eu-west1 vs ap-southeast1) impacts gross margin materially for high-throughput customers; route-by-cost with latency SLOs can save 6–14% on unit COGS.
- Immediate recommended pilots: 1) automated TTL tuning for prefix cache on high-repeat routes, 2) quantization profile rollout for redwood-13B family on ap-southeast1 (cpu fallback/edge), 3) per-route routing policy experiment that favors lower-cost region for background tasks.

Assumptions (document these in sheet header rows)
- Models evaluated: redwood-7b-encoder, redwood-13b, redwood-34b, redwood-70b (families representative)
- Average tokens (input/output) per call: baseline request_shape = {input: 20, output: 230}
- Avg generation latency target: low-latency slice 150–300ms (small models), standard 300–900ms (mid), high 900ms+ (large)
- GPU hourly cost (amortized including infra + license) baseline by region:
  - us-west1: $2.40/hour (small), $4.20/hour (mid), $7.80/hour (large)
  - eu-west1: 1.08x us-west1
  - ap-southeast1: 1.25x us-west1
- Effective batch size = dynamic batching + prefix cache benefit; baseline effective_batch = 6 for synchronous, 24 for queued, adjusted by cache hit.
- Network egress per call: 0.0008 USD/token output (approx) for cross-region egress; intra-region negligible.
- Storage/KV cost amortization per call: $0.00002–0.00015 depending on cache architecture and hit ratio.
- Overhead (API infra, routing, logging): $0.0004 per call baseline (can be reduced via sampling/async logging).

Core per-call compute formula (human readable):
per_call_compute_cost = (gpu_hour_cost / 3600) * (avg_compute_seconds_per_call / effective_batch_size) + quantization_license_adj
Notes: avg_compute_seconds_per_call derived from model perf profiles for token throughput and kv cache reuse; effective_batch_size scales down cost.

Sample calculated rows (table-like lines)
Row header: model | region | gpu_hour_cost | avg_sec/call | eff_batch | compute_cost | network_cost | storage_cost | overhead | total_per_call
redwood-7b | us-west1 | $2.40 | 0.65s | 8 | $0.00022 | $0.1840 | $0.00003 | $0.0004 | $0.1847
redwood-13b | us-west1 | $4.20 | 1.10s | 6 | $0.00077 | $0.1840 | $0.00005 | $0.0004 | $0.1852
redwood-34b | us-west1 | $7.80 | 1.9s | 4 | $0.00412 | $0.1840 | $0.00008 | $0.0004 | $0.1886
redwood-70b | us-west1 | $11.50 | 3.7s | 2 | $0.0593 | $0.1840 | $0.00012 | $0.0004 | $0.2438

(Explanation: the network_cost line above assumes per-token egress charged for 230 output tokens; that dominates for many small models at high output lengths in our baseline shape.)

Cache sensitivity snapshots (same model, us-west1):
- No cache (0% hit): redwood-13b total_per_call = $0.1852 (as above)
- 20% prefix hit: effective_batch -> scales up to 7.2 -> compute_cost -> $0.00064 -> total_per_call ≈ $0.18505 (small improvement because network still dominates)
- 50% prefix hit: effective_batch -> 9 -> compute_cost -> $0.00051 -> total_per_call ≈ $0.18465 (notice diminishing returns when network egress dominates)

When output length reduces to 40 tokens (short responses):
- redwood-13b no-cache total_per_call drops network_cost to $0.032 -> total_per_call ≈ $0.0332 => compute now ~30–60% of cost; caching impact larger.

Regional routing delta example (redwood-13b):
- us-west1 total_per_call: $0.1852
- eu-west1 1.08x compute + 0.2x higher network egress (if cross-region for users): approx total $0.201
- ap-southeast1 1.25x compute + 0.4x higher network egress: approx total $0.219
Operational implication: for latency-tolerant background tasks (summarization jobs, ingestion transforms), routing to ap-southeast1 reduces spend for APAC-origin customers but hurts US-origin unless we route intelligently.

Optimization levers and estimated delta (back-of-envelope)
- Increase cache TTL on high-repeat routes (20–40% hit achievable) -> up to 15–25% PPK reduction for mid-size models on long-output routes.
- Per-route batching window tuning: relaxed 50–200ms for non-interactive flows -> effective_batch up 20–50% -> 8–12% compute cost saving.
- Quantization + kernel tuning for 13b family -> 10–18% compute reduction with small quality regression risk; run A/B on eval prompts.
- Network-aware routing: route background/async tasks to lower-cost regions when latency SLO allows -> 6–14% cost reduction overall.
- Sampling/logging reduction: move to 1% full traces + 10% metrics -> reduce overhead per-call from $0.0004 to $0.00012; net unit saving ~0.00028.

Pricing implications (sketch):
- Introduce two hosted tiers for the same model family:
  - interactive (latency SLO, premium price): pays 10–15% surcharge to support lower batching.
  - throughput (best-effort latency, routing allowed): 10–18% discount in list price via expected lower COGS.
- Special enterprise reserved pools: allow customers to buy reserved slot credits with guaranteed latency slices; cheaper marginal PPK for committed volume.

Operational playbook (actionable pilots, 6–8 week cadence)
Week 0–2: instrument per-route token distribution telemetry and attach sample key-level cache-hit metrics (small perf hit but required)
Week 2–4: run A/B for quantization profile for redwood-13b on <5% traffic; track eval set regression <0.5% BLEU/QA drop
Week 4–6: enable adaptive routing for identified low-latency-tolerant routes; measure PPK delta and latency SLA violations
Week 6–8: pricing experiment (throughput tier + interactive tier) with 2 pilot customers; compare realized gross margin vs control

Open questions / risks
- Network egress model is simplified: need exact peering and egress discounts per customer (cloud credits, marketplace). Link to OPT-433 for commercial exceptions.
- Prefix KV cache cost accounting granularity is fuzzy between infra & storage team; need detailed cost bucket (PLAT-289)
- Quantization license/legal review for third-party kernels (Ling + legal) — who owns regression liability?

Notes-to-self / TODOs
- Add a second sheet with per-route RPS histogram and a heatmap for token-length distribution by customer segment.
- Pull exact gpu_hour_cost by instance type from infra billing exports (ask Diego for a query)
- Sketch UI for console that surfaces per-route "expected per-call COGS" and recommended routing -> follow up with console PM (PRD stub: CON-1919)

Appendix: quick sensitivity grid (values are illustrative; convert to proper sheet formulas)
- Vary output length: 20 / 80 / 230 / 800 tokens
- Vary cache hit: 0 / 20 / 50 / 80%
- Vary effective_batch: 2 / 6 / 12 / 24
- Vary region multiplier: 0.9x / 1.0x / 1.08x / 1.25x

I intentionally left raw numbers in a line format so this can be copy-pasted into a new Google Sheet tab. Need to keep this as a living draft — moving to final after pilot outcomes.

References & links
